title: Keyboard Manager new interface exits unexpectedly.
author: jdraggy

status.label: Likely covered by the self-contained editor fix
status.detail: The logs and later discussion match the Keyboard Manager WinUI 3 launch crash that upstream PR #49524 fixed by building the editor self-contained and that issue #49399 later confirmed resolved on 0.101.2211.

next_action.label: Point to the self-contained editor fix and ask for a retest
next_action.reason: There is already a concrete upstream fix path with later confirmation on the same editor-launch family.

judgment.rationale: The uploaded logs, later Windows App Runtime symptom, and current repository history all line up with the WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor launch crash fixed by upstream PR #49524. A closely related issue (#49399) was later confirmed resolved on 0.101.2211.
evidence: The original issue says the new Keyboard Manager UI process appears and exits without showing a window.
The attached bugreport logs show the WinUI 3 editor failing to load Powertoys.KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper.dll and then failing to initialize the mapping service.
A later commenter says Windows first reported a missing Windows App Runtime component and then the editor still failed to open.
Current repository history shows PR #49524 explicitly fixes the new Keyboard Manager editor launch crash by building it self-contained.
Closed issue #49399 documents the same editor startup family and was publicly confirmed fixed in prerelease 0.101.2211.
judgment.recommended_action: Point the report to #49524 and ask for a current-build retest rather than opening a second Keyboard Manager startup investigation.

fix_assessment.rationale: A concrete upstream fix exists for the WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor startup failure family.

issue_context.summary: The new Keyboard Manager editor exits during startup, and the attached logs plus later Windows App Runtime symptoms align with the launch-crash family already fixed by the self-contained editor change in #49524.
known_information: The reporter is on PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store on Windows 10 19045.6066.
The original report says PowerToys.KeyboardManagerUI.exe appears and exits without showing a UI.
Two PowerToysReport ZIPs are attached across the issue and follow-up comment.
A maintainer comment quotes logs showing Powertoys.KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper.dll missing and the mapping service failing to initialize.
A later commenter reports a missing Windows App Runtime prompt followed by a silent failure.
inferences: The live symptoms all sit in the WinUI 3 editor startup and dependency-loading path rather than in remap logic after launch.
The later Windows App Runtime note and the current self-contained build fix strongly suggest the report belongs to the same launch-crash family already fixed on main.
issue_context.analysis: Current upstream history provides a stronger ownership signal than a new design would: there is already a focused editor-startup fix, plus a public confirmation on a closely related issue. The right action is to route this report to that fix and request a current retest.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, all comments, labels, assignees, and both bugreport attachment references.
Downloaded and unpacked the first PowerToysReport ZIP and confirmed the WinUI 3 editor log contains the missing KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper.dll and mapping-service initialization errors.

Inspected upstream history for the new Keyboard Manager editor and found PR #49524, which fixes the launch crash by building the editor self-contained; also reviewed closed issue #49399, where a later commenter confirmed the prerelease resolved the crash.

actions.label: Point to self-contained editor fix #49524

comment.body: Thanks for the logs and the follow-up details. The missing WinUI 3 editor startup is now tracked by the self-contained editor fix in #49524, and the closely related launch-crash issue #49399 was later confirmed fixed in the 0.101.2211 prerelease. Please retest with a current build that includes #49524 and confirm whether the new Keyboard Manager editor still exits immediately or still reports a missing Windows App Runtime component.
